A closed form is a great way to make a lidded jar! Here are a few helpful tips:  • poke a small hole so that as it dries and shrinks, air can release safely. • push in your flange on a straight edge, not a curve. • you don’t have to have a knob on top. You can go knobless or even add on a handbuilt knob after trimming. • stay tuned for next week’s tutorial Tuesday where I show you how to trim this into a lidded vessel! #tutorialtuesday #potterytutorial #ceramics #ceramictutorial #potterytiktok #wheelthrowing #liddedjar

There’s gonna be a lot of pretty great monsters in the batch. I feel like I’m honing in on my glazing techniques and my construction is getting better and better. Sometimes I wonder if I’m stagnating because I’m working with in certain parameters, but also I feel like in terms of craftsmanship I’m growing. I’m really starting to realize how much you gain by repeatedly doing the same motions and repeatedly using the same general concepts… making these monsters has been such a great Zen like practice. I’ve never really appreciated or understood production pottery or how you could make the same bowl or the same mug, and while this isn’t really that I am using some of the same building techniques the basic thing stays the same, and then it’s really just variables that create these characters, and I’m kind of enjoying the practice of it. #vermontartist #ceramics #scarymonster #kilnreveal

lidded jar tutorial - part 1 (throwing the jar body and lid)✨ have to break this up into 3 parts because it will take weeks to go through the steps (we're making these jars in real time and rely on a community studio to fire) and I simply can't fit throwing, trimming, and glazing the jars into one reel 🥲 i find 200g is perfect for throwing the small jar body, plus another 150g for the lid. you'll see i throw my jar body and lid separately, leaving a lot of the refining for the trimming stage. especially with the lids, I find it easier to throw them roughly and finesse the fit once they're leather hard. i don't wire off the lids or jars, i wait until they pop off the bats. xo shan #pottery #potterytutorial #liddedjar #handmadeceramics #canadianartist

These single piece jars are a piece I’ve been making for quite a while now and they’re really fun method for creating a lidded jar. The first step is to collar in and enclose a shape while maintaining a rounded form. The second part is to apply pressure at the wall using a small cut piece of a credit card or a small flat tool to make a ridge. Careful to not just remove clay, you want to press inward, making an inner flange for the lid. Once the piece is leather hard, I use a flat knife to cut the top and bottom apart at the base of the ridge. I then trim the gallery for the inside of the base and ensure that the lid flange fits inside it snuggly. #pottery #studioceramics #wheelthrown #handmade #potteryartist

Pottery is usually shared in fast forward, but this process felt worth slowing down for. I’ve been experimenting with slip & and handmade resist templates lately, and I can’t get over the texture and pattern that emerges when everything comes together. There’s something so satisfying about peeling away the template and seeing the design revealed for the first time. This piece still has a few more steps before it’s finished, but I’m already obsessed with where it’s headed. In this Tips video I go over how I cut my pieces off of the hump. I’ve seen quite a few different techniques from various potters on this process, but I’ve found this to be what works for me. I can’t stress enough practicing the technique before committing to trying to make pots to alleviate a lot of the frustration that can come from figuring it out. I think a lot of people give up on it because of this and as we all know, persistence pays off in ceramics. I hope this video helps and I’ll keep making them…If anybody’s interested in learning more about these techniques I do have a workshop coming up in January at Jewell Town Pottery in Massachusetts. Feel free to give them a shout and inquire about availability.                                          #potterytips #learning #ceramics #pottery #wheelthrown
